newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends rangebound session lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends rangebound session lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures broadly weaker and toward session lows in rangebound trade Friday, pressured by speculative and light trade selling, floor sources said.

Prices headed lower from the outset on the heels of overnight losses in the London cocoa market. Active March slipped through near-term chart support at $1,370 a tonne, but traders said losses were capped by steady manufacturer-related buying.
March futures ended $13 a tonne lower, at $1,367, having ranged from $1,375 to $1,366. May fell $9, to $1,393, while the rest finished $9 to $10 weaker.

Traders said news that UK-based PCR Ltd managing director Robert Fish said Thursday the Ivory Coast's total cocoa production in the 1996/97 season is likely to be at least one million tonnes could have weighed on the market.
"I think the forecast may have shook out a few specs," one trader said.
On the charts, near-term support was seen at $1,362-$1,367 in the March contract, followed by $1,350. Resistance was pegged at $1,375-$1,378, a gap on the charts.
